temporal_identity_hash.prior_behaviour: readProjectedUniverseAsOf() never threw on zero rows; a whole-system-empty universe (no listing known to the platform at all as of the cutoff) hashed to a real-looking 64-character string via hash([[], []]), confirmed by a ground-truth capture against a minimally-seeded world (calendar+config only, no tickers/listings at all).
temporal_identity_hash.genuine_absence_vs_valid_empty: listing existence is not a per-date business outcome the way trading-day status is (a listing does not stop existing because today happens to have no session); a genuinely empty universe is therefore always a gap, never a legitimate value -- unconditional on trading-day status.

calendar_status_hash.prior_behaviour_calendar_half: sessionContext() already throws MARKET_CALENDAR_EVIDENCE_MISSING when zero calendar rows exist for the date -- an existing, upstream guard, now proven executing (not merely read) by a new test that deletes the calendar row and asserts the throw.
calendar_status_hash.prior_behaviour_status_half: resolveForListing() never throws; it returns a named unknown()/no-evidence sentinel (status_code=UNKNOWN, a specific reason_code) per listing when no override exists. This is the common, correct default for the overwhelming majority of listing-days -- most listings have no special status revision most days -- and is itself distinctly represented in the hashed content, not indistinguishable from real data the way a fabricated hash would be.
calendar_status_hash.classification: calendar half: ALREADY_PROVEN_BY_EXECUTING_UPSTREAM_GUARD (newly proven executing in this unit). status half: not a required-input-missing concern; no fix needed.

event_factor_hash.prior_behaviour: zero corporate-action revisions and zero factor sets for a trade date is the common, legitimate outcome (corporate actions are rare events); confirmed by code inspection (no minimum-cardinality requirement exists anywhere in this domain) and the same ground-truth capture, which returned a real hash of an entirely empty structure without incident.
event_factor_hash.genuine_absence_vs_valid_empty: no counterpart of is_trading_day (or any other signal) exists that says 'a corporate action was expected today' -- every trade date can legitimately show zero, so there is no discriminating 'genuine absence' distinct from 'correct absence' to construct a test for.
event_factor_hash.classification: authority permits legitimate empty; not a required-input-missing concern; no fix needed and no discriminating probe is constructible

source_observation_manifest_hash_and_can.prior_behaviour: neither method throws on zero rows (only on a missing knowledge_cutoff); a trading day with nothing recorded at all -- distinct from a recorded provider outage, which SourceObservationAsKnownBoundaryTest::test_zero_row_provider_outage_remains_in_as_known_observation_manifest already proves is legitimately observation_count=1 with a SOURCE_TIMEOUT reason -- hashed to a real-looking value and was admissible. Confirmed by a ground-truth capture: a seeded listing with zero md_source_observations rows produced a valid 64-character manifest_hash with observation_count=0.
source_observation_manifest_hash_and_can.genuine_absence_vs_valid_empty: a non-trading day legitimately has zero observations to record -- the same distinction ExpectedBarDecisionService::decide() already draws via EXPECTED_BAR_NON_TRADING_DAY, an existing, established precedent in this exact codebase, not an invented rule. Gated on calendar_context.is_trading_day.
source_observation_manifest_hash_and_can.classification: IMPLEMENTATION_DEFECT, fixed in this unit, conditional on trading-day status
